701666.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“thus, so”), probably as a grammaticalization of the sense "to fit, fix". Cognates include Lithuanian ir̃ (“and; so”).

701635.t: From ἀποφθέγγομαι (apophthéngomai, “I plainly speak my mind”), from ἀπο- (apo-, “away”) + φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to speak loudly”), + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

701693.t: Pre-Greek origin, although related to Latin arānea. Whether it is the source of the Latin term or they both originated from a different common source is unclear.

701622.t: From ἀπο- (apo-, “away, from, off”) + τρέπω (trépō, “turn”) from Proto-Indo-European *trep-.

701665.t: Arcadocypriot Greek καταρϝος (katarwos, “cursed”) suggests a preform Proto-Hellenic *arwā, which makes Attic -α hard to explain; -η would be expected after *w. Not cognate with Latin āra (“altar”).

701613.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂ep Proto-Indo-European *-o Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó Proto-Hellenic *apó Ancient Greek ἀπό (ăpó) Ancient Greek ἀπο- (ăpo-) Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- Proto-Indo-European *dʰédʰeh₁ti Ancient Greek τίθημι (títhēmi)…

701633.t: From ἀπο- (apo-, “away from”) + φεύγω (pheúgō, “to flee, run off”).
